subject: Post-demo: usage thresholds, budget floor, and provisional credit bridge
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@novalegal.ai>, Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@novalegal.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: usage thresholds, budget floor, and provisional credit bridge

Hi Samantha / Marco —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our demo and the pricing/credit conversation so we have a clean next-steps list: 

What we heard (NovaLegal current plan):
- Target workload: document summarization + entity extraction across 3M tokens/day at peak (batch inference, 99th pctl SLA 350ms).
- Expected steady-state token consumption: 200–600k tokens/day for the first 90 days while models and prompts iterate.
- Budget range: initial monthly spend range $8k–$25k (depending on throughput and model family).

Redwood recommendation / unit economics discussed:
- Baseline unit price target: $1,800 per 1M input+output tokens (projected using their preferred quantized model and 0.5x batching).
- Suggested safety floor: reserve a 10% buffer on daily burst capacity to avoid throttling during court filing windows.

Provisional credits we can offer (conditional):
- One-time trial credit: $6,000 (applied to your Redwood account; equates to ~3.3M tokens at the baseline rate).
- Credit validity: 60 days from activation.
- Condition: a short mutual action plan (MAP) signed via the HubSpot link below outlining goals, target success criteria, and a single integration milestone (API + basic KV caching).

Next steps (agreeable to both teams):
1) Samantha to confirm expected peak tokens/day and any non-standard latency windows (reply by EOD Tue).
2) We (Marissa + Ben) to share a simple MAP and the credit activation form once we have an internal approval (target by Mon 6/2).
3) Laura (ops) will draft a recommended autoscaling policy for the Dedicated/Disk-backed KV cache to keep unit cost near the $/1M target.

Attachments: Novalegal_trial_plan_v1.pdf (proposed MAP), usage_estimate_sheet.xlsx (token model).

If that all looks right, reply with a quick confirmation and the single sentence that should go into the MAP for success criteria (e.g., "reduce manual review time by 40% for first-pass redlines").

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0197

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@novalegal.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: usage thresholds, budget floor, and provisional credit bridge

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Quick replies inline: 

- Peak tokens/day: our current spike tests hit ~2.6M tokens/day for heavy litigation batches; normal business days are ~250–400k tokens/day. The spike windows matter — they last ~2–3 hours on filing days.
- Budget: our procurement team has an initial approved pilot budget of $10k/month. We can stretch to $15k/month if we have firm unit economics and predictable throttling behavior during spikes.

We appreciate the provisional credit offer. Two asks before we sign the MAP: 
1) Can the credit validity be extended to 90 days? Our legal review calendar is slow and procurement needs the extra runway.
2) Can you put an explicit SLO for throttling behavior during the 2–3 hour spike windows (we need either guaranteed capacity or an automatic fallback to a slightly cheaper model variant to avoid failures)?

If you can confirm those two items we can provide the single-line success criteria and loop in procurement to accept the MAP next week.

Thanks —
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Product 
NovaLegal.ai
samantha@novalegal.ai

Hi Samantha — appreciate the quick clarity. Short answers and a finalized offer below.

1) Credit validity: we can extend the trial credit to 90 days (one-time exception approved by Revenue Ops).
2) Spike SLO / fallback: we will commit to a managed fallback policy — during sustained spikes we will automatically route to an approved compatible variant with up to 20% higher latency but 40% lower unit cost. If that fallback is used more than 3 days in any 30-day window, Redwood will schedule a capacity review and provide a one-time emergency credit equal to 5% of the monthly burn during the incident window.

Final conditional offer:
- One-time credit: $6,000, valid 90 days from activation.
- MAP: we will share a 1-page MAP link; signing opens credit activation (signature by a NovaLegal product owner).
- Acceptance criteria: single-line success metric from NovaLegal + confirmation of expected peak windows in writing.

Ben and Laura are looped for operational review; Laura will follow up with the recommended autoscaling policy and a short appendix that maps the fallback variant to expected $/1M token impact. Ben — I flagged this for finance so we can auto-apply the credit once MAP is signed.

Action items:

- Laura: drop autoscaling & fallback appendix by Mon 6/1.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you into a trial.
